params.body:
Ilse, 23 September 2026, for Garage De Ro: he can pick the Spoticar warranty and save it, but on his return the field is empty again, so the vehicle is not published on Spoticar. Only vehicles entered after the update; the older ones keep theirs.

## What it was

The five warranties live in the shared partial `_tabs/general.blade.php` as plain radios with a hidden zero beside each. The classic sheet posts that. The Livewire sheet includes the same partial but posts no form, and nothing bound those radios, so the choice never reached the save. No error, no trace.

It costs more than an annoyance: Spoticar publishes a vehicle only with fifteen photos **and** a stated warranty, so those cars stood nowhere at all.

Counted across the eleven dealers with `has_spoticar_warranty` on, by day:

```
09-04 : 12 vehicles, 12 with a warranty
09-08 :  9 vehicles,  8
09-10 :  5 vehicles,  4
09-11 :  1 vehicle,   1
09-16 :  1 vehicle,   0   <--
09-17 :  2 vehicles,  0
09-18 :  6 vehicles,  0
09-22 :  4 vehicles,  0
09-23 :  1 vehicle,   0
```

Fourteen vehicles, none with a warranty, from the day after the cutover of 15 September. Her three (intern 293, 273 and 277) are in there, entered on 18 September and edited again that morning between 09:14 and 09:58: the dealer trying once more.

## The fix

The choice hangs on one property carrying the column name, and is translated back into the five columns on save, exactly as the classic sheet posts them. The partial gained an `$lw` branch, like the descriptions already had.

The fourteen existing vehicles do not repair themselves: only the dealer knows which warranty belongs on each. Now that the choice sticks, setting them once is enough.

## The guard, because this is the second time in two days

Nederland Mobiel fell out of the sheet the same way yesterday (#760). So the test is on the shape rather than on these two fields: `EveryFieldOfTheSheetIsSavedTest` walks every partial the Livewire sheet includes, takes each form field that carries no `wire:model`, and requires `VehicleForm` to know the name, as a property, in `wiredKeys()`, or as a key it writes.

It swept the whole sheet while being written and found two more names, both legitimate and now listed with their reason: `total_price` shows a computed sum and is no column, and `available_on_stocklist_date` is calculated by the sheet itself rather than posted. Two fields outside the included partials were checked by hand and are fine: `favorite_available_on_stocklist_date` is derived in `OwnStockService`, and the rest of `dates.blade.php` is reproduced in the sheet's own markup.

Verified locally: 26 tests, 85 assertions across the two new tests, the Nederland Mobiel test and the rule-catalogue tests.
params.title: The sheet keeps the Spoticar warranty, and a test keeps every other field
